lines: The clock rang, so I finally woke up
Yesterday's cold feels almost like a lie
Even if I wanted to go out, ah
the forecast says rain
Either way, nothing will come out because the night won't end
A dry throat, an aching heart—
all of being human is in the way
At the speed of goodbye, lift your face
Someday, once the night finally breaks, then
wake up and look
at you with your sleepy eyes
I'll keep drawing you, over and over
I take out an umbrella and finally decide to step outside
but wait—didn't I throw out my shoes?
There's no way I'd have the nerve to go out still barefoot
Maybe it doesn't matter. What do I even want to do?
What about dinner? If it clears up, I'll go outside
People—I don't even want to look at them, but
swimming through today at this same speed
once my hand finally touches you, then
wake up and look
at you with your sleepy eyes
Even if I forget, I'll remember
You're there before the hill. It's been so long, you say
laughing, you lean your face close
Come on, let's go together, you say
Under a barn in Lapland
On the old streets of Gamla Stan
The summer grass gets in the way
Swimming through today at this same speed
once my hand finally touches you, then
wake up and look
at me, who forgot you
At the speed of goodbye, lift your face
Someday, once the night finally breaks, then
wake up and look
at you with your sleepy eyes
I'll keep drawing you, over and over
